plain_english: Under the Conservative Joint Policy (Disparity detected if either Alg 1 or Alg 2 rejects H0), the global federated model exhibits statistically significant performance disparities across clients at alpha = 0.05. Alg 1 p-value: 8.2572e-07, Alg 2 p-value: 1.4421e-06.

alg1_result.null_hypothesis: H0: mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_K = mu (Equal client performance)
alg1_result.alternative_hypothesis: H1: mu_i != mu_j for some i != j (Performance disparity exists)
alg1_result.interpretation: The test statistic T1 = 45.2605 exceeds the critical value at alpha = 0.05 (p = 8.2572e-07 < 0.05). We reject the null hypothesis of equal client performance. There is statistically significant evidence of cross-client performance disparity.

alg2_result.null_hypothesis: H0: mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_K = mu (Equal client performance)
alg2_result.alternative_hypothesis: H1: mu_i != mu_j for some i != j (Performance disparity exists)
alg2_result.interpretation: The Welch-type test statistic F = 4.9961 with df = (9, 810.4) is significant (p = 1.4421e-06 < 0.05). We reject H0. Even after accounting for unequal variances, there is strong evidence that the model does not perform equally across clients.
